story: The Salt Lake Temple is a temple of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, on Temple Square in Salt Lake City. It was dedicated in 1893 after being constructed over a period of 40 years. At 382,207 square feet, it is the largest Latter-day Saint temple by floor area.

The center pinnacle rises 210 feet to the base of the angel Moroni statue. The large baptismal font is mounted on the backs of twelve oxen, like the Molten Sea in Solomon's Temple. Latter-day Saints consider the temple sacred, and a temple recommend is required to enter, so there are no public tours inside.

The first public photographs of the interior were published in 1912. The temple closed in 2019 for remodeling, including a seismic retrofit. The church plans public open house tours in 2027, after which it will be re-dedicated.

story: The Beehive House was built in 1854 and was one of the residences of Brigham Young, the second president of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Its name comes from the beehive sculpture on top. Early Mormons used honeybees to symbolize industry and cooperation.

Truman O. Angell, Young's brother-in-law and the architect of the Salt Lake Temple, designed it. It is built of adobe and sandstone. It served as the executive mansion of Utah Territory. A suite of rooms connects it to the neighboring Lion House, and Young died in his bedroom there in 1877.

After Young's death it passed through disputes among his heirs and later served as a boarding house for women. It is normally a historic house museum, but it has been closed for renovation since 2023, with a reopening expected in 2027.
stops.fact: Young died in the house in 1877.
stops.disputed: Many people think the name means real bees lived here. Wikipedia says the name comes from the sculpture on the roof.

story: Brigham Young built the Lion House in 1856, two years after the Beehive House. Truman Osborn Angell was involved in the design. It is a Gothic Revival mansion with 20 gables for 20 small bedrooms.

It is named for a statue of a lion, sculpted by William Ward III, above the front entrance. Lion of the Lord was a nickname for Young. It is joined to the Beehive House by a series of rooms that Young used as offices, and it housed many of his wives and children.
Later it held the domestic science department of LDS University in the 1920s and became a social center in the 1930s. It closed in 2020 and is being restored, with reopening expected in spring 2027.
stops.fact: It has one gable for each small bedroom.
stops.disputed: Many people think the house is named for a real lion. Wikipedia says it is named for a statue above the entrance.

story: The Eagle Gate is an arch across State Street at its intersection with South Temple. It honors Brigham Young's 1859 gate, which was an entrance to his property and the City Creek Canyon road. The tolls for hauling wood from the canyon could be paid by giving Young every fifth load.
After the road was opened to the public and the gates removed, the arch with its eagle and beehive stayed. The structure has been rebuilt twice, in the 1890s and the 1960s.

The current bronze eagle was made in the early 1960s and has a wingspan of 20 feet. It weighs 4,000 pounds. The arches and pillars are a steel frame covered in metal panels, and Wikipedia calls the design one of the city's finest examples of mid-century modern.
